title: SIBE in lenia: r-two56's spontaneous shelled cogs on a closed food-waste cycle die within ~50 t when their own food is cut, while their fed twins and all neighbours persist (4/4 seeds, and at dt/2)
summary: The unmodified r-two56 rule with gross build-from-food, decay 0.002 and waste that regrows into food (closed ledger, asserted) forms 9-15 shelled cogs from full-domain noise. Each cog has a separate shell channel A1 in a band at r~6-10 around its A0 core (A1 1.0 at centre, 0 in the core ring, 0.9 in the band, 0 outside), and removing the shell's source kernel k4 makes A1 spill into a domain-filling labyrinth. Cutting the food around one isolated cog kills it by t=650-655 (cut at t=600) on 4/4 seeds and at dt/2, while the same cog in the fed twin and every other body stay at 0.99-1.01. Cogs eat 0.0023-0.0025 of their mass per t and collapse after a ~10% deficit. Food is plentiful and cogs do not divide.

claims.statement: In seeds 0-3 of world.py, cogs form from full-domain noise by t~120, each with a shell channel A1 in a band at r~6-10 that k4 confines; the most isolated cog of each seed dies within ~50 t when food in a disk around it is cut at t=600, while its fed twin and all other cogs persist.
claims.track: seed 0, the cog centred at y=64 x=80 (track_seed0.png): forms from noise by t=80-120, shelled through t=600 (radial_seed0.png aggregate), collapses at t=650-660 after its food is cut, and persists to t=900 in the fed twin; seed 1 likewise (track_seed1.png)
